owner.occupation: Youth ice hockey coach (Canadian, at an international school)

world.bio: Canadian youth ice hockey coach working at an international school in Qingdao. From Winnipeg, played junior hockey, now teaching PE and coaching. I want to start a weekend club for local kids who can't afford gear. Learning Mandarin tones with a tutor app, missing my dog back in Winnipeg, home-brewing beer in my apartment.
skills_assets: Level 2 Hockey Canada coach, 11 years coaching youth hockey
A personal bag of equipment: skates, sticks, helmet, pads
School gym and a small off-ice training room I can use on weekends
WeChat group of 31 parents from the school, plus 12 local families who signed up for the weekend club
Contact at a local sports shop which gives a discount on used gear
Experience of outdoor rinks and pond hockey in Manitoba

projects.name: Qingdao Weekend Hockey Club
projects.text: Posted: 'Twelve local kids signed up for the weekend club. Zero ice time, zero gear.' Kids are aged 7 to 12, from a nearby community, none of them has ever stood on skates. Parents are willing to pay 100 RMB a month at most. I've inspected three rinks; mall rinks quoted me 1,500 RMB an hour, far beyond what the parents can pay. I want weekly ice time for twelve kids, ideally Saturday mornings. The school's insurance only covers indoor rinks, and I've never worked on natural or river ice.

projects.name: Gear donation drive
projects.text: Emailed a hockey shop in Winnipeg and the team I used to play for. Received promise of 15 used helmets and 10 pairs of skates, shipping unresolved.

projects.name: Home brewing
projects.text: A red ale in a fermenter on top of the fridge. Smells promising. I'm learning Chinese words for 'hops' (啤酒花).

notes.text: Walked past a mall rink in Shinan today. Kids' public skating, 80 RMB each. Found out private ice time is 1,500 an hour, minimum two hours. For twelve kids weekly that is 12,000 a month. No parent can afford that.
Mandarin tutor: 'Mā, má, mǎ, mà.' I said all four and he said 'wrong'. I said 'all four?' He said 'yes'. Have I wasted six months?
Mum phoned: Dad has to retire. His knees. He's 68. I can feel Winnipeg slipping away. The dog, Gus, has a new friend at my sister's place.
Principal asked about the club. I said 'We have kids, no ice.' She said 'Insurance only covers indoor rinks.' I said 'I know.' She said 'Let's find indoor then.' Fine, but indoor is expensive.
Tried on-ice coaching with a few international school kids at the weekend. They're lovely but they all have their own gear. I want the ones who don't.
Brewed a second batch. Mistake: too much specialty malt. Ended up with a stout that tastes like burnt toast. Drank it anyway.
Two local parents came to the school gym to watch an off-ice session: pushing a sled, stickhandling with tennis balls. One mum said 'He is very patient.' I'm learning the word 耐心.
Got a message from a Qingdao hockey group on WeChat: 'ice time available Wednesday 6am.' Wednesday 6am? Kids have school. Replied politely.

messages.text: Lin: Today, 'ice' in Chinese. Me: 冰. Lin: Good. Now 'hockey'. Me: 冰球. Lin: Perfect. Me: Finally something I know.
Karen: Dad's having his knee done Dec 5. Me: I'll try to come. Karen: Gus misses you. Me: He's a dog, he doesn't know. Karen: He sleeps on your old hoodie.
Mrs. Wang: My son loves the sticks. Me: He's got great hands. Mrs. Wang: How much per month? Me: 100 RMB. Mrs. Wang: We can do that. Me: Thank you.
Shop: We have 15 helmets for you. Me: Fantastic. Shop: Shipping to China is 900 CAD. Me: Hmm. Shop: Let me ask.

calendar.event: Off-ice session with club kids, school gym, 9am

relations.about: Supportive but cautious about insurance and liability.
Parent of one of the club kids, practical and enthusiastic.

constraints: Parents can pay maximum 100 RMB per kid per month
School insurance covers indoor rinks only
Needs bilingual communication, English or simple Chinese
sensitive: Father's knees; feels guilty about being far away
Salary is decent but he sends money home
